messages.content: Write the first page of an onboarding document for a new backend engineer joining a payments team. Around 200 words.

Payments Team Onboarding

You're joining the team that moves money for the company. Every checkout, refund, and payout runs through code you'll now own a piece of. That comes with a different bar than most backend work. A bug here doesn't just break a page; it can charge someone twice or leave a merchant unpaid. Read this before you write your first line.

What we own. The payments service handles charge creation, refunds, payout scheduling, and reconciliation against our processor (Stripe). It's a Go monolith backed by Postgres, with a Kafka queue for async settlement events.

Your first week. No code changes yet. Get read access to the payments repo, staging dashboard, and the #payments-oncall Slack channel. Shadow one on-call rotation. Read the postmortems in docs/incidents. They teach you more about our failure modes than any design doc.

Ground rules. Every change touching money paths needs two reviewers, one of them senior. Idempotency keys are mandatory on any endpoint that moves funds; if you're not sure whether yours needs one, ask. We test against the processor's sandbox before every deploy and never skip it.

Your onboarding buddy is assigned in the welcome email. Reach out anytime. Local environment setup follows on the next page.
Add a section on who to ask for what.

Who to ask for what

Your onboarding buddy is the first stop for code review and architecture questions. For on-call and production incidents, post in #payments-oncall and don't DM individuals — someone is always watching that channel. Processor integration questions (API quirks, sandbox behavior, webhook signing) go to #stripe-integration, where several people have direct contact with Stripe's support team. Finance-eng owns reconciliation and ledger discrepancies; they run the nightly reconciliation job and can tell you if a mismatch is expected or a bug. Ask compliance questions (PCI scope, what you can log, what you can't) before you guess — ping #payments-compliance. File access requests (prod database, processor dashboard, secrets) through the IT portal linked in the welcome email; don't ask a teammate to share credentials directly.

If you're not sure who owns something, ask in the team channel rather than guessing. Nobody expects you to know the org chart in week one.

Add a short note about the on-call rotation.

output:
On-call

You'll join the on-call rotation after your first shadow week, once your buddy signs off. Rotations run one week at a time, and the schedule lives in the payments-oncall calendar linked in #payments-oncall on Discord. Primary carries the pager; secondary backs them up and takes over if primary can't respond within 15 minutes. Every incident gets a postmortem in docs/incidents, written up within 48 hours regardless of severity.
